Context/Background:
Circular RNA (circRNA) is a class of noncoding RNA with regulatory potentials. Here, we identified circRMST as an exceptionally abundant circRNA predominantly expressed in neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC), with strong conservation between humans and mice.

To explore the functional role of circRMST, we designed two shRNAs targeting the backspliced junction (BSJ), achieving 70%–93% knockdown efficiency. In 3D Matrigel-embedded cultures, circRMST knockdown significantly impaired cell growth across three NEPC and four SCLC-A models. Additionally, cell cycle analysis in SHP77 cells revealed cell-cycle arrest. In vivo, SHP77 xenografts in NSG immunodeficient mice exhibited markedly reduced tumor growth upon circRMST depletion.
Prompt:
To investigate transcriptional changes following circRMST knockdown, we performed RNA-seq in SHP77 cells and identified hundreds of differentially expressed genes.

What are the most relevant pathways in a GSEA results with the differential gene list?  Nominate a target most relevant for neuroendocrine prostate cancer.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
CircRMST is a circular RNA highly expressed in neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) and small‐cell lung cancer, with knockdown in SHP77 (NEPC) cells leading to cell‐cycle arrest and impaired 3D growth. RNA-seq following two independent shRNAs in SHP77 cells yielded ~6,000 overlapping genes with consistent log₂FC. Differential expression (mean log₂FC) was used for preranked GSEA across KEGG_2016, GO_Biological_Process_2023, Reactome_Pathways_2024, and MSigDB_Hallmark_2020. Hundreds of pathways were significant (FDR<0.05 for some Hallmark and Reactome terms; broader FDR<0.5 for others).

Keywords  
circRMST; neuroendocrine differentiation; proteostasis/ER stress; mTORC1 signaling; GPCR signaling

Candidate Genes  
MTOR; RHEB; ASCL1; SESN3; CDKN1A

Pathway Enrichments

• GO_Biological_Process_2023: 200 up, 101 down (total 301)  
• Reactome_Pathways_2024: 125 up, 45 down (total 170)

Analysis  
circRMST depletion drives a coordinated induction of proteostasis and lysosomal pathways (Protein processing in ER, N-glycan biosynthesis, Lysosome), metabolic reprogramming toward mTORC1 activation (Amino Acid–Regulated mTORC1, Hallmark mTORC1 Signaling) and cell‐cycle progression (Mitotic Spindle), while suppressing neuroendocrine lineage programs (Neuroactive ligand–receptor, Neuron Differentiation, GPCR Signaling). The pronounced upregulation of multiple mTOR‐related gene sets (Hallmark mTORC1, Reactome “Amino Acids Regulate mTORC1”) alongside leading‐edge genes MTOR, RHEB, SESN2/3, MTOR emerges as a central hub linking metabolism, growth, and differentiation signals in NEPC.

Target Nomination  
Based on GSEA, MTOR is the most compelling candidate: it appears in leading edges of three distinct mTOR‐related sets (mTORC1 Signaling, Amino Acids Regulate mTORC1, Energy Dependent Regulation of mTOR by LKB1-AMPK). As a druggable kinase with established relevance in prostate cancer growth and lineage plasticity, MTOR represents a strategic target for NEPC following circRMST knockdown.

Next Steps & Clarifications  
1. Validate MTOR activation status (phospho‐S6K, p4EBP1) in circRMST‐depleted SHP77 xenografts.  
2. Test sensitivity of NEPC models to mTOR inhibitors (e.g., everolimus) ± circRMST knockdown.  
3. Assess ASCL1 re‐expression for rescue of neuroendocrine phenotype to confirm pathway suppression.  
4. Examine whether ER stress modulators (e.g., 4-PBA) alter mTOR activation or growth arrest post-circRMST depletion.
